claim: When the RNG or LD A,R depends on timing, neutralise it in both test copies (make it constant, LD A,I, or NOP the seed step) and cover every R read, or build and original play different games.

evidence.text: The RNG runs in the wait-for-interrupt sound loop, so any timing change gives other enemies; the first pace runs left it in and diverged at update 3; a fixture removing that call and the lives decrement in both copies kept lockstep at every update.
evidence.quote: the RNG runs in the wait-for-interrupt sound loop, so any timing change gives other enemies;

evidence.text: Original and build drift apart through the ISR's RND seed; a test-only fixture (BA58 INC HL made NOP in both) keeps whole pace runs in lockstep.
evidence.quote: Original and build drift apart through the ISR's RND seed; a test-only fixture (BA58 INC HL made NOP in both)

evidence.text: LD A,R at 15 places decides the elves' moves and R also runs in a HALT, so play is timing-dependent even in the original; a test fixture with those reads constant keeps state in lockstep.
evidence.quote: R: LD A,R at 15 places decides the elves' moves; R also runs in a HALT, so real play is timing-dependent even in the original.

evidence.text: The RNG at 82D0 reads ROM bytes (LD A,R, XOR (HL)) that differ between 128K ROM 1 and Sinclair's, so the build's random spawns differ from the original's; a fixture makes it constant for lockstep.
evidence.quote: LD A,R and XOR (HL) over bytes of the ROM's first page, which differ between 128K ROM 1 and Sinclair's (004A), so the build's random spawns are not the original's.

evidence.text: The game takes LD A,R (0x9466) for its randomness, so JNext runs of two builds play different games; pace by seed varies -25% to +18% over 8 seeds; the replay pace is the like-for-like figure.
evidence.quote: so JNext runs of two builds play different games (port 0xFE writes 106 against 179): pace by seed varies -25% to +18%.

evidence.text: The first LD A,R list came from code that ran; a scan of the whole snapshot found a third read; a pace fixture has to cover all of them.
evidence.quote: The first LD A,R list came from code that ran; a scan of the whole snapshot found a third read.

next_check: A pace profile key "fixture" of byte patches applied to both copies, with a scan that lists every LD A,R the fixture does not cover.
